parsed.explanation: The operative regime criminalises same-sex conduct (up to eight years plus lashes) and same-sex marriage, framed by sex with no guidance on how trans persons classify — an open but consequential question for an outed trans visitor. Enforcement is sparse (one documented 2015 arrest, no state complicity found in 2020), so severity-if-outed is moderate-high, not catastrophic: prosecution and lashes are possible, execution is not per the record's legal analysis. Trans-specific exposure is undocumented; the UN agency's report of hate crimes against people 'perceived as transgender' is the main trans-specific negative, plus pervasive stigma, no protections, and restrictive official posture (60 rejected UPR recommendations). Resorts offer a documented partial haven, but its legal basis is unresolved. Thin-data criminalising state with no relief record resolves to high-risk band, not elevated-criminalisation tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented: no passport-marker rule, screening procedure or documented entry friction for trans visitors; classification of trans persons under sex-based offences unstated.
entry_documents.protection: Travel guidance reports LGBTQ tourists generally welcome at private tourist resorts.
entry_documents.interaction: Criminal statutes govern conduct and marriage, not documents, so entry exposure is unknown rather than evidenced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Same-sex conduct offence up to eight years plus lashes applies to all persons since 2014; trans classification under sex-framed provisions is unresolved; one documented 2015 arrest from a private home after public complaint.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Sparse documented enforcement; 2020 report found no official complicity in abuses against LGBTI persons; no capital punishment for these offences.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A public complaint could trigger investigation of an outed trans visitor; custodial conditions for trans detainees not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, bathroom, ward or custody-placement rule for trans persons documented.

care_services.exposure: No care restriction documented for visitors; hormone access, import rules and emergency-care treatment of trans persons unknown.
care_services.interaction: Uncertainty about whether presenting trans status while seeking care triggers the conduct provisions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State rejects trans-inclusive UPR recommendations (60 rejected as contradicting Islamic faith/Constitution), rejected SOGI resolutions, opposed decriminalisation; asylum statement threatened prosecution on return; homosexuality a social taboo, online defenders harassed as apostates.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 foreign-government report found no documented official complicity in abuses.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility is climate-level; enforcement documented only once.

minors_guardians.exposure: Same-sex marriage offence (one year) could engage a couple travelling with a child whose relationship is read as same-sex; Sharia provisions affect children born outside marriage.
minors_guardians.interaction: No custody or family-separation rule documented for trans visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: UN agency reported hate crimes and human-rights violations against people perceived as homosexual or transgender; 2013 neck stabbing of a gay blogger; pervasive stigma likely suppresses reporting; 2024 expert survey lists LGBTQIA+ people among the most at-risk groups.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No anti-discrimination law or hate-crime recourse; government noted but rejected reform recommendations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence undocumented; reporting likely discouraged.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal protection against gender-identity or sexual-orientation discrimination; no documented relief mechanism; whether the Penal Code applies at resorts is expressly unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Resort islands documented as generally welcoming and described as outside religious law, though not legally established.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data: absence of later enforcement cases does not establish present safety; remedies absent if outed outside resort zones.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia documents routine, systematic police stops and coercive interviews of trans visitors as state practice; this dossier documents no trans-specific targeting and one criminalisation arrest, but adds a heavier latent statute (eight years plus lashes) and stronger official hostility. Severity-if-outed is comparable; the missing trans-specific enforcement keeps it near this anchor.

Caldera shows active undercover sweeps, blackmail and prosecution spikes; here enforcement is a single 2015 incident with no complicity findings, and no documented trans targeting. The latent conduct statute and pervasive stigma track this anchor's structure, but the much lower documented enforcement frequency argues for sitting slightly above it.

Kestrel Isles harms are administrative (delays, refused entry) with written remedies; here the consequence if outed is potential criminal prosecution with lashes and no functioning remedy, materially worse. But this jurisdiction documents no routine traveler-facing exposure at all, while 0.55-B's screening is universal — so this sits below it.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a criminalising regime whose provisions are sex-framed and unresolved for trans persons, backed by pervasive societal stigma, documented hate-crime risk against people perceived as transgender, and a state that rejects trans-inclusive reform at every international forum. Mitigating this: enforcement is sparsely documented (one 2015 arrest), no official complicity or trans-specific targeting is recorded, capital punishment is excluded by the record's legal analysis, and resort zones offer a documented (if legally unresolved) welcoming space. No trans-specific law, document rule or facility rule exists to create universal exposure. Thin-data extrapolation from structure — criminalisation, religious-law governance, no protections, no relief record — supports high risk; the absence of any documented traveler-facing trans exposure prevents severe-tier placement. 0.33: high risk, well short of organised-targeting regimes, elevated above acceptance-with-gap jurisdictions.
